note: Every measurement Isobath has published, with its sample, method and stated limits. REFUTED entries are never removed. Each has a page at /findings/<id>.html

findings.title: Free collateral cannot be derived from position and margin data; naive arithmetic misclassifies one wallet in five
findings.observation: withdrawable == accountValue - totalMarginUsed for 19% of wallets; 20% misclassified as able to defend
findings.sample: 74 Hyperliquid wallets holding open BTC positions, queried live 2026-08-20
findings.method: compare venue-reported `withdrawable` against marginSummary arithmetic on the same response
findings.confidence: single venue, single moment, wallets already known to hold positions; would be strengthened by repetition across days and by a second venue
findings.market_gap: no provider checked (HyperTracker, Coinglass, 0xArchive, Tardis, QuickNode, Dwellir, PurrData) exposes this field

findings.title: Order-book depth falls as price moves get larger, so a static-book cascade estimate is optimistic
findings.observation: near-book depth falls to 0.8462 at a 5-minute horizon during the largest moves (p25 0.6573), against 1.0015 in quiet markets
findings.sample: BTCUSDT, 1,324 days (2023-01-01 to 2026-08-19), 3,733,943 snapshots, 0 missing days; largest bucket n=313 across 160 distinct days
findings.method: notional within +/-1% after a window divided by before, bucketed by absolute move, de-overlapped at the horizon
findings.confidence: quiet-market control reads 1.000 to four decimals across 1,320 days, so the effect appears only where claimed; one venue, one asset
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product models a non-static book

findings.title: A properly aged wallet universe sees 53.3% of Hyperliquid BTC open interest, not 20%
findings.sample: 31,349-wallet universe; stratified estimate with a random sample of 1,200 of the 25,954 newly discovered wallets
findings.method: known stratum from the last deep scan plus mean-per-wallet extrapolation over the new stratum; bootstrapped interval
findings.confidence: still a lower bound — the universe is activity-derived and the recording keeps discovering wallets
findings.market_gap: no provider publishes a coverage figure for position data

findings.title: The wallet universe is exhausted; more wallets of the same kind would add nothing
findings.observation: claimed 20.24% coverage was near the ceiling; actual is 53.3%
findings.sample: the claim rested on a universe frozen after FOUR HOURS of recording, documented as 21 days
findings.method: n/a — the error was a premise never measured, not a calculation

findings.title: Daily-horizon directional tests on one instrument cannot detect realistic edges; the region is unpowerable, not empty
findings.observation: detecting a 52% hit rate needs 4,900 independent days (13.4 years); 51% needs 19,600 (53.7 years)
findings.sample: standard power arithmetic applied to the project's own recorded sample sizes
findings.method: 80% power, alpha .05 two-sided, on a proportion, with observations counted as INDEPENDENT rather than raw
findings.confidence: arithmetic, not an estimate; the only judgement is what effect size counts as realistic

findings.title: Binance order-book behaviour under stress transfers to Hyperliquid
findings.observation: none — nothing has been measured on Hyperliquid
findings.confidence: untested and load-bearing; hl2 began recording Hyperliquid l2Book at nSigFigs=3 on 2026-08-20 to settle it

findings.title: No provider sells per-wallet account state, so an archive of it is a durable moat
findings.observation: HyperTracker sells it — complete market coverage, 15-20 minute snapshots, history from 2025-04-04, $179-1,999/month
findings.method: n/a — the claim was asserted from landing pages rather than docs
findings.confidence: refuted from the vendor's own field list

findings.title: The position map is up to an hour stale relative to the order book, which manufactures phantom triggers
findings.observation: clock gap of 3,055 s (51 min) between the latest l2Book snapshot and the latest position snapshot
findings.method: compare observation timestamps of the two joined sources
findings.confidence: structural, not incidental -- the fast position scan runs hourly while the book updates every 5.3 s
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product discloses the age of the positions behind its map

findings.title: Visible forced flow on Hyperliquid BTC is small relative to visible book depth
findings.observation: $63.6M total forced selling in the visible map against $222.5M of bids within 2.71% of mid; a $10.6M trigger moved price 0.069%
findings.sample: one snapshot pair, 2026-08-20, fast-tier map at 24.2% coverage
findings.method: cascade sweep of the observed ladder against the observed book, evaporation not applied
findings.confidence: ONE observation, low coverage, static book, and a 51-minute clock gap (F-0008)
findings.market_gap: no product publishes forced flow as a ratio to available depth

findings.title: Forced liquidation does not move price more than a volatility-matched random minute in the same hour
findings.observation: 15m mean +40.07 bps in the forced direction against a matched control of 44.52 bps; no horizon clears both benchmarks
findings.sample: 228 independent episodes >=$250k across 28 symbols (n=106 with price data), Binance market-wide, 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-20
findings.method: CASCADE-1, contract frozen sha256 7dee22eed9cdaecb before any outcome; episodes not events; permutation null plus same-symbol same-hour control
findings.confidence: K1 met at 228 episodes, so this is not an underpowered null; three days, one venue, and only two of four declared benchmark tiers were implemented
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product publishes a volatility-matched control

findings.title: The hourly map systematically under-represents the positions closest to liquidation
findings.observation: deep scan (5,395 wallets): median distance to liquidation 15.5%, 42.8% of positions within 10%. Fast scan (top 300 by notional) at the same period: median 31.6%, 23.0% within 10%.
findings.sample: one deep snapshot of 1,327 BTC positions against three fast snapshots of 267-270, 2026-08-21
findings.method: distance to liquidation as |liquidationPx - spot| / spot, per position, compared across scan tiers
findings.confidence: one deep snapshot against three fast ones, same day, single venue, single asset. Needs several deep/fast pairs across different market conditions before it is more than PRELIMINARY.
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product we surveyed states which population its map is drawn from, let alone how that population biases the result

findings.title: The vulnerability figure Isobath publishes is very nearly a constant, so it cannot discriminate between clusters
findings.observation: across 433 published clusters, cannot_defend_pct has median 100.0 and 71% sit at exactly 100%. Splitting at the median leaves 29% below and 0% above. thinly_defended_pct behaves the same: median 100.0, 27% below, 0% above.
findings.sample: 433 clusters published across 23 hourly and deep snapshots, Hyperliquid BTC, 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-21
findings.method: contrast pre-condition P1 of market/CONTRACT-calibration.md, run before any outcome was examined
findings.confidence: three days, one venue, one asset, and drawn largely from the fast scan tier whose selection bias is F-0011. A market regime with materially lower leverage could restore the spread. What is not in doubt is that no spread exists in the period recorded.
findings.market_gap: no liquidation product publishes a defensibility figure at all, so none has had occasion to discover that theirs would not vary either

findings.title: Wallets holding free collateral leave the market more often than trapped ones, so disappearance cannot be read as liquidation
findings.observation: across 4 deep-to-deep transitions, of wallets within 5% of liquidation: 62.7% of those WITH free collateral were absent at the next scan, against 45.1% of those with none. The sign is opposite to the hypothesis that free collateral aids survival.
findings.sample: 2,302 wallet-transitions within 5% (3,331 within 10%) across 5 deep scans of the frozen 5,395-wallet universe, Hyperliquid BTC, 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-21
findings.method: track each wallet's BTC position between consecutive DEEP scans only; classify as absent, survived-improved or survived-worsened; split by whether withdrawable was above zero
findings.confidence: only 4 transitions, 12.9h apart, so wallets are counted repeatedly and these are not independent observations. One venue, one asset, 54 hours. The direction is clear; the magnitude is not established.
findings.market_gap: no provider publishes wallet-level survival at all, because none archives per-wallet account state over time

findings.title: Both venues' ±1% BTC book holds roughly a quarter of a billion dollars, so a single sweep costs about 1 bp at retail size and a typical liquidation cluster is too small to move price
findings.observation: standing notional within ±1% of mid is $247.6M median on Binance futures and $225.6M median on Hyperliquid — within 9% of each other. At burst level, a same-side sweep worth 0.5–1% of that book costs the taker 0.8–1.1 bps of slippage. The median published liquidation cluster is 0.44% of the Hyperliquid book; the p90 cluster is 5.1%.
findings.sample: 221,778 aggressive bursts ≥ $50,000 over 2 Binance futures days (2025-03-10/11), joined to bookDepth ±1%; 5,112 Hyperliquid l2Book snapshots 2026-08-20/21; 433 published clusters
findings.method: contiguous same-side aggTrades within 200 ms grouped into one burst; cost = executed VWAP against the price at which the burst began, signed against the taker; conditioned on the PREVIOUS minute's range so that volatility already in progress cannot be credited to the burst
findings.confidence: two Binance days and 34 hours of Hyperliquid book. The order of magnitude is not in doubt; the day-to-day variation is not established, and neither is behaviour in a stressed regime, where F-0002 measured near-book depth falling to 0.657
findings.market_gap: liquidation heatmaps publish cluster notional without ever stating it as a fraction of the book standing in front of it, which is the only form in which the number means anything

findings.title: How a liquidation price responds to added margin cannot be derived from Hyperliquid's published state, so the "add $500 and your liquidation moves to X" feature cannot be built from arithmetic
findings.observation: the documented formula reproduces the venue's own liquidationPx to within 10 bps for only 56.4% of cross positions (median error 4.79 bps, n=1,019); inverting it position-by-position within a single account recovers margin_available values that disagree by 3.49% at the median and 73.7% at p90, so only 28.2% of accounts are internally consistent within 1%
findings.sample: 90 Hyperliquid accounts fetched live 2026-08-22 (1,474 positions, 1,019 cross); 39 accounts holding 2+ cross positions; 1,923 wallet-transitions across 6 deep scans
findings.method: liq_px = entry - side*margin_available/|szi|/(1 - l*side) with l = 1/(2*maxLeverage), margin_available = crossMarginSummary.accountValue - crossMaintenanceMarginUsed; then the same formula inverted per position and compared within each account; then the implied derivative compared against observed liquidationPx movement in wallets whose position size was unchanged
findings.confidence: one venue, one afternoon, 90 accounts. The three checks disagree with the formula in three different ways, which is stronger than any one of them; but the third conflates unrealised PnL with deposited collateral and cannot yet isolate a real deposit
findings.market_gap: no provider offers a margin-response figure at all, and this measurement suggests why -- the obvious arithmetic is wrong in a way that only shows up in the tail

findings.title: Across six years, none of nine public market-state variables separates forward trading conditions once trailing realised range is held constant
findings.observation: band-controlled lift for all nine candidates sits between 0.914 and 1.129 in raw form, and z-scoring each against its own 30-day history collapses every one toward 1.000 (1.129 to 1.039, 1.126 to 1.052, 0.914 to 0.964). The raw long/short lift reverses sign by year: 1.170, 0.990, 0.948, 0.869, 1.164, 1.232, 1.178 for 2020 through 2026
findings.sample: 66,397 hours of BTCUSDT, ~51,000 usable per candidate; Binance 5-minute metrics from 2020-09 joined to 1-minute klines
findings.method: outcome is realised range over the following 24h; control is realised range over the previous 24h, banded; inside each band the candidate is split at its own median and the ratio of median forward ranges taken, then averaged across bands by weight
findings.confidence: 24h windows stepped hourly overlap ~24-fold, so the effective sample is nearer 2,000 than 51,000 and a residual lift of 4-5% is far inside the noise. One venue, one asset, one horizon, one outcome family. A screen, not a pre-registered test — its authority is only to eliminate
findings.market_gap: none. Every variable here is public and anyone could run this; that it has apparently not been run is not the same as it being ours

findings.title: In a uniform random sample of Hyperliquid BTC traders, ten wallets hold 57% of the leveraged exposure and the median position is $1,308
findings.observation: of 8,000 wallets drawn uniformly at random from 51,765 discovered, 2,249 held a BTC position totalling $222.9M. The top 1 wallet holds 14.0%, the top 10 hold 56.6%, the top 100 hold 87.6%. Median position $1,308 against a mean of $99,108 — a mean 76 times the median
findings.sample: WIDE-1 first scan, 8,000 wallets, Hyperliquid BTC, 2026-08-22
findings.method: uniform random sample without replacement, seed 20260822 recorded before drawing, from every distinct wallet seen in the BTC trade recording; positions read from the venue's own clearinghouse state
findings.confidence: one scan. Concentration through time is the question worth asking and this is a single point on it. The draw is uniform over wallets that TRADED BTC during the recording window, which is not the same as uniform over all Hyperliquid accounts
findings.market_gap: every provider reports aggregate open interest. None reports how few accounts it belongs to, because none holds an unbiased per-wallet sample

findings.title: The hourly scan reproduces coverage and forced notional to within a point, but sees only 28% of positions near liquidation where the full scan sees 47%
findings.observation: across 7 deep scans paired with the fast scan nearest in time, coverage agrees to within 1.6 points (36.8% vs 36.2% on the closest pair) and forced sell-side notional within ±12%; but median distance to liquidation is 11.6% in the deep tier against 26.5% in the fast tier, and the share of positions sitting within 10% of liquidation is 47.4% deep against 27.8% fast
findings.sample: 7 deep/fast snapshot pairs within one hour of each other, 10,585 deep positions and 1,896 fast positions, Hyperliquid BTC, 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-22
findings.method: pair each deep snapshot with the fast snapshot closest in time; compare the published aggregates directly, and compare the full distance-to-liquidation distribution of the positions each tier actually holds
findings.confidence: three days, one venue, one asset, 7 pairs. The direction is unambiguous and consistent across every pair; the exact ratio is not established. The earliest pair sat at 20% coverage while the archive was still filling and its forced-notional gap (71.3M vs 33.6M) is far larger than any later pair's
findings.market_gap: no provider states which of its published figures survive its own sampling and which do not

findings.title: Holding trade size against the standing book fixed, a book thinner than three-quarters of its own daily normal costs about 20% more — so the ratio absorbs most but not all of the stress regime
findings.observation: across 985,950 aggressive bursts, median cost at a burst/depth ratio of 0.01-0.02 is 1.88 bps when the book is below 0.75x its day's median, against 1.62, 1.54 and 1.62 bps in the three deeper regimes. The pattern repeats at every ratio band: 0.98 vs 0.80-0.83 at 0.005+, 3.24 vs 2.58-2.74 at 0.02+. Only the thinnest band separates; the other three are indistinguishable
findings.sample: 985,950 same-side aggressive bursts of $50,000 or more, 22 days sampled every 60 days across Binance futures BTCUSDT from 2023-01-01 to 2026-06-14, joined to bookDepth within ±1%
findings.method: contiguous same-side aggTrades within 200 ms grouped into one burst; cost is executed VWAP against the price at which the burst began, signed against the taker; depth regime is the standing ±1% notional divided by the same day's median, so the split is "thin for this market" rather than "thin for 2023"
findings.confidence: the daily-median regime is not the same stress F-0002 measured, which was depth AFTER a large move relative to before — a sharper and rarer condition this test does not isolate. Bursts within a day are not independent. The high-ratio cells above 0.05 remain empty, so nothing is established about large trades
findings.evidence: market/impact2.py run_stress, market/CONTRACT-impact.md K4, research/QUEUE.md Q6
findings.market_gap: every execution model assumes a static book; none states whether its own estimate survives the regime where it would be used
